evidence.role: The official leaf establishes use of the pressure definition inside a hydrostatic derivation; this retrieval wording is original.

hints: Recall how the previous lesson described the direction of the force relative to the surface as well as how it is spread.
After writing p = F/A, undo the division by A with the same operation on both sides.

walkthrough.text: Use the controlled wording: pressure is normal force per unit area.
Write p = F/A.
Multiply both sides by A to obtain F = pA.

ai_rubric.observable: States that pressure is normal force per unit area
Rearranges p = F/A to F = pA

evidence.role: Both official derivations require the chain V = Ah and m = ρV; the diagnostic options and values are original.

hints: Build the column volume first from its base area and height.
Rearrange density as mass equals density multiplied by volume, then compare the options.

walkthrough.text: The straight column volume is V = Ah.
From ρ = m/V, rearrange to m = ρV.
Substitute V = Ah to get m = ρAh, so option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the column mass as m = ρAh

evidence.role: The mapped derivations cancel area after combining weight and pressure; the proportional-area diagnosis is original.

hints: Imagine doubling only A while keeping density and depth fixed. Track what happens to ρAhg.
Then track the denominator in p = F/A and look for a common factor.

walkthrough.text: At fixed ρ and h, the column weight ρAhg is directly proportional to A.
Pressure divides that weight by the same base area A.
The two proportional changes cancel, so option C is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that column weight and base area scale together, so A cancels in pressure

evidence.role: The official column derivations use vertical liquid height; the curved-route contrast is an original misconception probe.

hints: In Δp = ρgΔh, interpret the h symbol geometrically rather than as distance travelled through a pipe.
Compare the vertical coordinates of R and S and ignore how the connector bends between them.

walkthrough.text: The formula uses Δh, the difference in vertical depth.
S is 0.40 m vertically below R, so Δh = 0.40 m.
The 1.2 m curved route does not affect hydrostatic pressure difference, so option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects the 0.40 m vertical depth difference rather than the curved path length

evidence.role: These official leaves require a complete density-to-weight-to-pressure derivation. This vessel wording and assumption prompt are original.

hints: Begin with the geometry: write the volume of the liquid above the base using A and h, then use density to replace mass.
Turn mass into weight before dividing by the same area A. Keep the assumption separate from the algebra.

walkthrough.text: The liquid volume is V = Ah.
From ρ = m/V, m = ρV = ρAh.
The column weight is W = mg = ρAhg.
Use pressure as force per area: Δp = W/A = ρAhg/A = ρgh.
State that the liquid is static or that its density is uniform.
Check the unit: kg m⁻³ × N kg⁻¹ × m = N m⁻² = Pa.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses V = Ah with ρ = m/V to obtain m = ρAh
Uses W = mg to obtain the liquid-column weight ρAhg
Uses pressure as force divided by area and cancels A to obtain Δp = ρgh
States a valid assumption that the liquid is static or has uniform density

evidence.role: The official evidence derives surface-to-base pressure. This question extends the same controlled definitions to an original internal liquid-slab equilibrium proof.

hints: Treat pressure on each horizontal face as a normal force pA. Decide which surrounding liquid pushes upward and which pushes downward.
Write the slab weight from its volume AΔh. Use zero resultant force before cancelling the common area.

walkthrough.text: At the lower face, surrounding liquid pushes upward with force p₂A.
At the upper face, surrounding liquid pushes downward with force p₁A.
The slab volume is AΔh, so its mass is ρAΔh and its downward weight is ρAΔhg.
Equilibrium gives p₂A = p₁A + ρAΔhg.
Cancel A and rearrange to p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh.
A different imaginary area changes every force in the same proportion, so it cancels and cannot change the pressure difference.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies p₂A upward at the lower face and p₁A downward at the upper face
Identifies the slab weight ρAΔhg acting downward
Uses equilibrium and rearranges to p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh
Explains that all forces scale with the same area A, which therefore cancels

evidence.role: Mapped evidence establishes the derivation demand. The two-level diaphragm context, numbers and force calculation are original and combine current learning with the previous pressure lesson.

hints: Before using the numbers, write the same three-force equilibrium for an imaginary oil slab between the connection levels.
After finding the pressure difference, return to the previous lesson and rearrange pressure as normal force per unit area. The higher-pressure oil pushes toward the lower-pressure side.

walkthrough.text: For an imaginary slab of area A, the lower pressure force p₂A acts upward while p₁A and the weight ρAΔhg act downward.
Equilibrium gives p₂A = p₁A + ρAΔhg, so p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh.
To three significant figures, Δp = 6.33 × 10³ Pa.
From the previous lesson, p = F/A, so the force from a pressure difference is F = ΔpA.
F = 6327.45 × 2.40 × 10⁻³ = 15.18588 N = 15.2 N to three significant figures.
The higher-pressure side produces the larger normal push, so the resultant is directed from that side toward the lower-pressure side.
Check: 6.33 kPa acting over about 0.0024 m² should give about 6.33 × 2.4 N = 15.2 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up the imaginary-slab equilibrium with pressure forces p₂A and p₁A and weight ρAΔhg
Cancels A and derives p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh
Substitutes 860 kg m⁻³, 9.81 N kg⁻¹ and 0.75 m into Δp = ρgΔh
Obtains Δp = 6.33 × 10³ Pa to appropriate precision
Uses F = ΔpA from the previous lesson's pressure relationship
Obtains 15.2 N and states that the force is directed from the higher-pressure side toward the lower-pressure side
